name: Isochronic staged gate-rate ramp: hold -> linear glide -> hold, phase-integrated so pulses never jump, raised-cosine edges, fixed carrier
goal: In-house (no YouTube source found after repeated hunts): ramp an isochronic tone's pulse RATE smoothly between two rates in stages (e.g. 12 Hz hold 4 s -> glide to 6 Hz over 12 s -> hold), by integrating the rate into the gate phase (phase = cumsum(rate)/SR mod 1) so the gate never restarts or skips mid-pulse; each pulse keeps raised-cosine edges (~4 ms, capped at half the on-time) so there are no clicks; carrier pitch never moves. Pairs with the binaural staged rate ramp already in this cluster.

source.title: In-house: iso_ramp() in sample-lab/theory/entrainment_tones.py (render: out/entrainment_gate_rate_ramp.wav)
source.transcript: none (in-house recipe, not distilled from a video)

prerequisites: DAW with an LFO/gate whose rate can be automated, or Python numpy/scipy for the reference generator

inputs.name: carrier_hz
inputs.description: Fixed carrier tone, e.g. 400 Hz or a chord tone of the track

inputs.name: duty
inputs.description: On-fraction of each pulse cycle, default 0.5

outputs.name: iso_ramp
outputs.description: Isochronic layer whose pulse rate glides between stages

constraints: Audio-craft only; no health or medical claims.
Rate changes only by gliding (no instant jumps); carrier pitch fixed (steady, no wobble).
Raised-cosine pulse edges, never hard gates: no clicks (Matt dislikes clicking textures).
Keep the iso layer under the pad (about -12 to -18 dB relative); drums, if any, still enter by ~8 counts.

steps.action: Pick a fixed carrier (a pad chord tone works; 400 Hz in the reference) and write the stage list: hold at the start rate, one linear glide, hold at the end rate. Keep glides >= 8 s for a smooth feel.
Build the per-sample rate curve by concatenating linear segments per stage.
Integrate the rate into the gate phase: ph = cumsum(r)/SR mod 1 (in a DAW: automate the LFO rate on a free-running, non-retriggering LFO so its phase carries across rate changes).
Gate shape: on for ph < duty; edges are raised-cosine ramps of ~4 ms, converted to cycles as edge*r and capped at duty/2 so fast rates still get a full on-plateau or a smooth bump.
Multiply the fixed-pitch carrier by the gate; render, then mix it under the pad.
steps.expect: Isochronic layer that slows (or speeds) smoothly

steps.action: Verify: count pulse onsets per 2 s window from a 60 Hz low-passed envelope; the counts should follow the stage plan (e.g. 12, 12, 11.5 ... 6.5, 6, 6).

verification: Onset counts per 2 s window match the planned rate within 0.5 Hz (reference render: 12,12,11.5,10.5,9.5,8.5,7.5,6.5,6,6).
No sample-to-sample jump larger than a carrier sine step (no clicks at gate edges).
Spectral peak stays at the carrier frequency throughout (fixed pitch).
